habitat: Singly in various wooded habitats, including suburbia.
summary: A common resident. Thick, stumpy bill with a pale patch at the base, yellow edges to the wing feathers, white outer tail feathers, a dusky breast and a white belly. The head is dull grey-brown, not greenish, with a dark grey malar stripe, and the underparts are not streaked. It calls tzeeu, then sheek repeated 30 to 40 times from a regular site. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Greater Honeyguide has a pale ear patch. The male’s bill is pink. Lesser Honeyguide has the pale patch at the base of a thick bill.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^13=8192 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 4096–16384.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

bill.shape: Thick and stumpy, with a pale patch at the base.

head.pattern: Dull grey-brown, not greenish. Dark grey malar stripe.

underparts.pattern: Dusky breast and white belly. No streaking.

wings.pattern: Wing feathers edged paler, with yellow edges.

viewNotes.note: Thick bill with a pale base, grey-brown head and white outer tail.
Pale patch at the base of the bill and a dark grey malar stripe.
The upper parts are dark on the colour line. The head is dull grey-brown.
Yellow edges show on the wing feathers.
Dusky breast and white belly, unstreaked.

calls.description: From a regular call-site, tzeeu, then sheek, sheek, sheek, repeated 30 to 40 times. Grade A call from near Richards Bay. The filename is a place name, Indaba Hotel R Bay, and does not name the bird.
